coverage_notes: Lemma lem:egf: Dirichlet integral and E X^alpha = alpha! verified; the generating function is correct as a formal power series (it diverges analytically, which is harmless). No issue.

Prop. prop:fibre: re-derived all cases (m(u')=0, m>=1, non-admissible, C_{m+1}-s<=g, R<=g, t=g boundary). theta and the J/I correction formulas are correct under the stated hypotheses; neither monotonicity nor g<C_1 is needed. The cap conditions g<C_m<=C_{m+1}<=C_m+g for m>=1 were checked exactly for all four cap sets, as were the failure at m=0 and Lemma 9.1 < Table 3 for every m.

V_D dimensions recomputed: 707, 846, 1041 for D = 20, 21, 22 (sum over even e of p(e/2)(D-e+1)). File coefficient counts match. The SY witness has 1311 power-sum terms; 1295 rows, every alpha nondecreasing with even parts, max a+|alpha| = 25.

Two-program claims checked exactly: I_T and J_T equal between check_* (capped_check) and res_* (capped_exact) for capfree_D20, opt49_D20r, kin48_D22r and ax45_D21. SY J_T is equal between check_sy236 and res_sy236_jonly. Theorem thm:240, Prop. prop:kin-own and Prop. prop:212 ratios recomputed. Piece counts 126 and 176 and core-hours 32.2 and 15.5 match the logs and checkpoints; 56 min matches.

Ceiling: logs show sigma=4 True and sigma=3985/1000 False (first run), and sigma=4 and 3990/1000 both True (recheck with loaded weights). The random vector is randint(-2^31, 2^31), so the Schwartz-Zippel bound 2/(2^32+1) < 2^-31 is correct. Optimum 3.98554779524. The is_pd recursion and the G_J error radius in capped_gram.py were read and appear sound.
Lean tuples: the 45/48/49/50-tuples of diameters 212/236/240/246 in Tuples.lean are sorted and admissible (Python check). No native_decide and no sorry; Audit.lean prints axioms. Lean was not built.
Remark rem:lemma5: the Lemma 5 / Lemma 3 reading matches notes/explorations.md (Session 10). The Kintali branch description matches notes/sources-236.md. Out-of-date relative to the audit: F01.

Not findings (minor exposition, left to other lanes): P* in Thm. thm:240(2) is defined operationally (the file P_opt49_D20r_u.json is the real definition); the counting lemmas are not 'used in Proposition prop:fibre' (folded into F02).

Earlier run referee/2026-11-13-verification-note (read after my own pass): C001, C002, C004, C008 and C009 appear fixed in v0.4. C003 is fixed for the SY digits, but the pattern persists at main.tex:388 (F07). C005(b) persists in part (F02). C006 persists as a provenance gap: the claim is now 'exact' and I verified it is true, but the cited files still do not record it (F03). C007 is superseded by v0.3/v0.4.

findings.title: The 'Lean-checked' counting lemmas are statements about lists of natural numbers, not about real points of L R_k or T
findings.analysis: lean/TwinPrimes/Caps.lean states every one of these for `l : List Nat` in integer units (1/1000, 1/2500, 1/1250), e.g. `stadlmann_large_count (l : List Nat) (h : forall x in l, 112 < x) (hs : l.sum <= 1042) : l.length <= 9`. Points of L R_k have real coordinates, and no rounding carries the real statement to the Nat one: flooring breaks the strict hypothesis 112 < x (x = 0.1125 gives 112), and taking ceilings breaks the sum hypothesis. So Lean checks an integer analogue whose content is the arithmetic 9*112 <= 1042 < 10*112. The real statements are true by the same one-line bound m*g < s <= L, which I re-derived for all six cases (1.042/0.112 = 9.30; 0.7596/0.0728 = 10.43; 1.06/0.0656 = 16.16; 0.442/0.112 = 3.95; 0.2824/0.0728 = 3.88; 0.548/0.0656 = 8.35, so j<=6 for s >= 777/1250). They are not what the kernel checked. Two further mismatches: (i) `charton_extra_le_six` assumes s >= 777 (the Table 3 C_1), so it does not cover the Lemma 9.1 support of Prop. prop:ceiling, where C_1 = 31/50 = 775/1250. The bound j<=6 still holds there, since (1325-775)/82 < 7. (ii) `kintali_extra_le_three` assumes s > 1899 strictly, while the J pieces with an admissible base have large mass >= C_{m+1} = 1899. The bound still holds. `charton_caps_valid` is the exception: it is an exact encoding, because the caps are integers over 1250. Line 515 also says these lemmas are 'used in Proposition prop:fibre', but the proposition uses none of them; they bound the ranges in the paragraph after it.
findings.suggested_fix: Label these range facts 'Proved here (elementary: m g < s <= L)' and describe the Lean lemmas as 'integer-unit analogues checked in Lean (the arithmetic only)'. Alternatively, restate the Lean lemmas over Int with hypotheses scaled so that they imply the real statements (e.g. for rationals with a common denominator). Note that the Cha26 extra-coordinate lemma covers the Table 3 caps only. In Reproducibility, change 'used in Proposition prop:fibre' to 'used in the inclusion--exclusion ranges after Proposition prop:fibre'.
findings.claim: Lean checks that at most 9 coordinates of a point of L R_49 exceed g, at most 10 large coordinates of a point of T for Kin26, at most 16 for Cha26, that inclusion-exclusion stops at j<=3,3,6, and (main.tex:314) that every point of T has all coordinates at most 0.6.

findings.title: The hedge 'not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its dimension' contradicts the project's own reading of Cha26 Sect. 11
findings.quote: result. We have not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its
findings.analysis: notes/stadlmann-recheck-s5.md:192-199 ('Basis and dimension (Sect. 11, p. 42): CONFIRMED') quotes Cha26: 'B21 = span_Q {(L - P1)^a P_lambda : a >= 0, lambda_j in 2Z>0, a + |lambda| <= 21}', with P_lambda a product of power sums (Sect. 9.4). This is the same family as V_21 (main.tex:254-255), and the span does not change under the rescaling u = 4t. The project's reading therefore identifies B_21 with V_21, up to the identification of their L with the support length; their fibre endpoint 'U(x) = min{L - S, max{g, C(s+1) - rho1}}' matches theta of Prop. prop:fibre. If the reading is right, Prop. prop:ceiling holds on the authors' own space, which is a stronger and simpler statement than 'a space of the size the authors use'.
findings.suggested_fix: State (Literature, read in the source) that [Cha26, Sect. 11] defines B_21 by the same generators, so V_21 = B_21. Then say that Prop. prop:ceiling holds for their space, keeping the caveat that their caps or L could differ from their Table 3. Otherwise, explain why the reading is not trusted.
findings.claim: The note only knows that Cha26's B_21 has the same dimension (846) as V_21.
findings.issue: The hedge 'not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its dimension' contradicts the project's own reading of Cha26 Sect. 11

findings.title: The ceiling's label and the results table do not say it is single-program and randomised-checked; its run provenance is incomplete
findings.location: Prop. prop:ceiling header main.tex:441; results table main.tex:112; text main.tex:450-461; Reproducibility main.tex:504
findings.analysis: The Gram weights are the reverse pass of capped_check.py, and they were validated only against capped_check.py: exactly at the input vector, and at one Schwartz--Zippel random vector (runs/gram45_rand_selftest.log). capped_exact.py was never run on the Lemma 9.1 support to completion (STATE.md:42; runs/exact_rand45_lemma91.log stops part-way). The proposition therefore rests on one program plus a randomised identity test, a status the note marks for other results ('two programs' / 'I_T one') but not in this label or table row; the caveat appears only in prose at main.tex:459-461. Provenance: runs/gram45_lemma91_D21.log and runs/gram45_lemma91_recheck.log record neither the precision nor the block split. The 6500-bit and 1/3-split values are stated only in STATE.md:41, and the 5000 bits only in the command in STATE.md:60. log/research-log.md:89 gives 4800 bits for the first sigma=4 certification. The saved weights were written to /tmp/claude-0/w45_lemma91.pkl and are not in the repository. I checked capped_gram.is_pd and the error radii of G_J (|error| <= colabs_i colabs_j + 1 in units of 2^-prec LQ^-2, from flooring); the logic is sound.
findings.suggested_fix: Label it '(Computed, ball arithmetic; weights from capped_check.py only, checked at a random point)' and mark the table row accordingly. Log the command line, precision and split in each gram run. Either commit the weights (or their hash and the regeneration command) or qualify the 'all inputs ... are in the repository' sentence. Reconcile the 4800/5000-bit record.

findings.title: Kintali comparison: '12 significant digits' understates the match, and 4.0030988047499... is rounded but printed with an ellipsis
findings.quote: and $J_T/J_0=0.99975643873\ldots$; ours agree with all four to $12$
findings.analysis: Kintali prints 33 digits (notes/sources-236.md:156-159), e.g. I/I_0 = 0.999890305383868079683497977904532... Exact recomputation from check_sy236.json, I0_sy236.json and J0_sy236.json gives 48J_T/I_T = 1.00077470118746844476347511150, 48J_0/I_0 = 1.00090870417598750570753733249, I_T/I_0 = 0.999890305383868079683497977905 and J_T/J_0 = 0.999756438739933773404567680739 (30 digits). These agree with all printed digits, so '12 significant digits' understates the match. Moreover, the quoted I_T/I_0 = 0.99989030538... shows only 11 significant digits. 4 x 48J_T/I_T = 4.00309880474987377..., whose 13-decimal truncation is 4.0030988047498..., so '4.0030988047499\ldots' is a rounded value written as a truncation. This is the same pattern the v0.2 changes say was corrected. All other ellipsis expansions in the note are correct truncations (checked: 4.0120389035, 4.0124198475, 4.0060814208, 4.0027351128, 4.00265968636, 1.0006649215907, 4.0030988047, 4.0036348167).
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'ours agree with all 33 printed digits of each' (or the true count), quote more digits of I_T/I_0 and J_T/J_0, and print 4.0030988047498\ldots.

issues.analysis: lean/TwinPrimes/Caps.lean states every one of these for `l : List Nat` in integer units (1/1000, 1/2500, 1/1250), e.g. `stadlmann_large_count (l : List Nat) (h : forall x in l, 112 < x) (hs : l.sum <= 1042) : l.length <= 9`. Points of L R_k have real coordinates, and no rounding carries the real statement to the Nat one: flooring breaks the strict hypothesis 112 < x (x = 0.1125 gives 112), and taking ceilings breaks the sum hypothesis. So Lean checks an integer analogue whose content is the arithmetic 9*112 <= 1042 < 10*112. The real statements are true by the same one-line bound m*g < s <= L, which I re-derived for all six cases (1.042/0.112 = 9.30; 0.7596/0.0728 = 10.43; 1.06/0.0656 = 16.16; 0.442/0.112 = 3.95; 0.2824/0.0728 = 3.88; 0.548/0.0656 = 8.35, so j<=6 for s >= 777/1250). They are not what the kernel checked. Two further mismatches: (i) `charton_extra_le_six` assumes s >= 777 (the Table 3 C_1), so it does not cover the Lemma 9.1 support of Prop. prop:ceiling, where C_1 = 31/50 = 775/1250. The bound j<=6 still holds there, since (1325-775)/82 < 7. (ii) `kintali_extra_le_three` assumes s > 1899 strictly, while the J pieces with an admissible base have large mass >= C_{m+1} = 1899. The bound still holds. `charton_caps_valid` is the exception: it is an exact encoding, because the caps are integers over 1250. Line 515 also says these lemmas are 'used in Proposition prop:fibre', but the proposition uses none of them; they bound the ranges in the paragraph after it.
issues.suggested_fix: Label these range facts 'Proved here (elementary: m g < s <= L)' and describe the Lean lemmas as 'integer-unit analogues checked in Lean (the arithmetic only)'. Alternatively, restate the Lean lemmas over Int with hypotheses scaled so that they imply the real statements (e.g. for rationals with a common denominator). Note that the Cha26 extra-coordinate lemma covers the Table 3 caps only. In Reproducibility, change 'used in Proposition prop:fibre' to 'used in the inclusion--exclusion ranges after Proposition prop:fibre'.
issues.claim: Lean checks that at most 9 coordinates of a point of L R_49 exceed g, at most 10 large coordinates of a point of T for Kin26, at most 16 for Cha26, that inclusion-exclusion stops at j<=3,3,6, and (main.tex:314) that every point of T has all coordinates at most 0.6.

issues.title: The hedge 'not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its dimension' contradicts the project's own reading of Cha26 Sect. 11
issues.quote: result. We have not checked that their space coincides with ours beyond its
issues.analysis: notes/stadlmann-recheck-s5.md:192-199 ('Basis and dimension (Sect. 11, p. 42): CONFIRMED') quotes Cha26: 'B21 = span_Q {(L - P1)^a P_lambda : a >= 0, lambda_j in 2Z>0, a + |lambda| <= 21}', with P_lambda a product of power sums (Sect. 9.4). This is the same family as V_21 (main.tex:254-255), and the span does not change under the rescaling u = 4t. The project's reading therefore identifies B_21 with V_21, up to the identification of their L with the support length; their fibre endpoint 'U(x) = min{L - S, max{g, C(s+1) - rho1}}' matches theta of Prop. prop:fibre. If the reading is right, Prop. prop:ceiling holds on the authors' own space, which is a stronger and simpler statement than 'a space of the size the authors use'.
issues.suggested_fix: State (Literature, read in the source) that [Cha26, Sect. 11] defines B_21 by the same generators, so V_21 = B_21. Then say that Prop. prop:ceiling holds for their space, keeping the caveat that their caps or L could differ from their Table 3. Otherwise, explain why the reading is not trusted.

issues.title: The ceiling's label and the results table do not say it is single-program and randomised-checked; its run provenance is incomplete
issues.location: Prop. prop:ceiling header main.tex:441; results table main.tex:112; text main.tex:450-461; Reproducibility main.tex:504
issues.analysis: The Gram weights are the reverse pass of capped_check.py, and they were validated only against capped_check.py: exactly at the input vector, and at one Schwartz--Zippel random vector (runs/gram45_rand_selftest.log). capped_exact.py was never run on the Lemma 9.1 support to completion (STATE.md:42; runs/exact_rand45_lemma91.log stops part-way). The proposition therefore rests on one program plus a randomised identity test, a status the note marks for other results ('two programs' / 'I_T one') but not in this label or table row; the caveat appears only in prose at main.tex:459-461. Provenance: runs/gram45_lemma91_D21.log and runs/gram45_lemma91_recheck.log record neither the precision nor the block split. The 6500-bit and 1/3-split values are stated only in STATE.md:41, and the 5000 bits only in the command in STATE.md:60. log/research-log.md:89 gives 4800 bits for the first sigma=4 certification. The saved weights were written to /tmp/claude-0/w45_lemma91.pkl and are not in the repository. I checked capped_gram.is_pd and the error radii of G_J (|error| <= colabs_i colabs_j + 1 in units of 2^-prec LQ^-2, from flooring); the logic is sound.
issues.suggested_fix: Label it '(Computed, ball arithmetic; weights from capped_check.py only, checked at a random point)' and mark the table row accordingly. issues.title: Kintali comparison: '12 significant digits' understates the match, and 4.0030988047499... is rounded but printed with an ellipsis
issues.quote: and $J_T/J_0=0.99975643873\ldots$; ours agree with all four to $12$
issues.analysis: Kintali prints 33 digits (notes/sources-236.md:156-159), e.g. I/I_0 = 0.999890305383868079683497977904532... Exact recomputation from check_sy236.json, I0_sy236.json and J0_sy236.json gives 48J_T/I_T = 1.00077470118746844476347511150, 48J_0/I_0 = 1.00090870417598750570753733249, I_T/I_0 = 0.999890305383868079683497977905 and J_T/J_0 = 0.999756438739933773404567680739 (30 digits). These agree with all printed digits, so '12 significant digits' understates the match. Moreover, the quoted I_T/I_0 = 0.99989030538... shows only 11 significant digits. 4 x 48J_T/I_T = 4.00309880474987377..., whose 13-decimal truncation is 4.0030988047498..., so '4.0030988047499\ldots' is a rounded value written as a truncation. This is the same pattern the v0.2 changes say was corrected. All other ellipsis expansions in the note are correct truncations (checked: 4.0120389035, 4.0124198475, 4.0060814208, 4.0027351128, 4.00265968636, 1.0006649215907, 4.0030988047, 4.0036348167).
issues.suggested_fix: Say 'ours agree with all 33 printed digits of each' (or the true count), quote more digits of I_T/I_0 and J_T/J_0, and print 4.0030988047498\ldots.
